newsitem.title: USA: NCAA AMERICAN FOOTBALL-WUERFFEL WINS HEISMAN TROPHY.
newsitem.headline: NCAA AMERICAN FOOTBALL-WUERFFEL WINS HEISMAN TROPHY.

text.p: Florida quarterback Danny Wuerffel followed in the footsteps of coach Steve Spurrier, winning the Heisman Trophy on Saturday as the outstanding U.S. college football player.

Wuerffel was presented the award at the Downtown Athletic Club, which annually awards the sport's most prestigious individual prize. He became the second Florida player to win the bronze statue, joining Spurrier, who won in 1966.
This season, Wuerffel led the nation with 39 touchdown passes and passed for 3,624 yards. He completed 207-of-360 passes and was intercepted 13 times.

The award capped a busy week for Wuerffel, who already had won the Davey O'Brien National Quarterback Award, the Maxwell Award as the nation's outstanding college player and the Honda Scholar-Athlete Award. On Friday night, he was named winner of the Johnny Unitas Award.

Wuerffel received 300 first-place votes and 1,363 points. Iowa State junior running back Troy Davis, the only player to rush for 2,000 yards in consecutive seasons, was second with 209 firsts and 1,174 points.

Quarterback Jake Plummer, who led Arizona State to an 11-0 mark, was third with 685 points (116 first-place votes). Ohio State offensive tackle Orlando Pace, who won the Outland and Lombardi Trophies as top lineman, had 599 points (87 firsts).

Wuerffel and Spurrier provide a sharp character contrast. The quarterback is quiet, respectful and deeply religious. The coach is cocky and arrogant and has developed a reputation for belittling his players in foul-mouthed explosions.

But for nearly four years, the pair were a perfect fit for the "Fun 'n' Gun" offence, instituted by Spurrier and executed by Wuerffel. The Gators have won four consecutive Southeastern Conference titles and Wuerffel has set 47 school, conference or NCAA records along the way.

Wuerffel was magnificent in Florida's only loss this season, 24-21 at Florida State. Under heavy pressure, he threw for 362 yards and three touchdowns. He scorched Alabama for 401 yards and six TDs in the SEC title game.

Davis carried 402 times, one short of the NCAA record held by Marcus Allen, for 2,185 yards and 21 touchdowns. Davis led the nation in rushing (198.64 yards per game), but his Cyclones won just twice in 11 games this season.

Plummer completed 57.2 percent of his passes for 2,575 yards and 22 touchdowns with nine interceptions. He engineered a stunning 19-0 upset of defending national champion Nebraska and numerous comeback victories for the Sun Devils.
